The release where an organization stops being one person. Since v1.2.0, RoboSystems App has gained real multi-user organizations — invite teammates, assign roles, and manage who can reach which graph — alongside two new surfaces: **Connect**, a one-page setup for pointing Claude and other MCP clients at a specific graph, and **Memory**, governance over what agents have remembered on your behalf. Usage reporting grew from a single storage number into a picture of where capacity actually goes, public pricing now names real numbers instead of pointing at a contact form, and the TypeScript SDK graduated from `0.4.0` to `1.7.0` underneath all of it.

## ✨ Organizations & access

- **Invite members and manage roles.** The Organization page's invite panel is no longer a placeholder: send an invitation by email and role, see pending invitations with resend and revoke, and watch a link lapse into an expired badge. Owner- and admin-gated, matching what the server enforces (#271)
- **Per-graph membership.** A **Members** entry on the graph dashboard opens the roster for the selected graph — explicit grants can be added, re-roled, or revoked, while org owners and admins are labelled _Via org role_ because their access is managed one level up. Shown to graph admins only, and never for shared repositories (#271, #272)
- **Graph creation is an admin action.** Members now get an explanation of who in their organization can create a graph, instead of a CTA that would be refused (#274)
- **Billing lives with the organization.** `/billing` is gone as a standalone page; Billing, Subscriptions and Invoices are peers of Graphs and Members in the organization tab row, addressable via `?tab=`. The old URL 307s to the new one, so Stripe return URLs and API upsell links keep working. The payment-portal button is owner-only rather than a 403 waiting to happen (#273, #275)
- **Your org ID, where you need it.** Surfaced on the organization page for graph limit requests (#221)

## 🔌 Connect: MCP without the local bridge

- **New `/connect` page.** For the graph you have selected, one **Generate** action mints a graph-scoped API key and fills in every snippet at once — the claude.ai connector URL, the `claude mcp add` command for Claude Code, and the `mcp.json` entry for Cursor and VS Code. Switching graphs switches the page and resets to placeholders, so one graph's credential is never shown under another's name (#282, #284, #285)
- **The npx stdio bridge is retired from the recommended path.** Every graph is reachable over the remote transport at a single URL, and the onboarding, landing, platform and open-source surfaces were rewritten to say so. `@robosystems/mcp` remains supported and is labelled as the stdio bridge for proxy mode (#282, #288)
- **Scoped keys at mint time.** The Settings create-key dialog gained an optional graph-scope selector — account-wide stays the default — with copy explaining that connector URLs accept only scoped keys, plus a pointer to `/connect` (#286)
- **SEC repository onboarding** now mints its key scoped to that repository and shows the same three snippets (#284)
- Corrected the curl and Python examples on the getting-started page (#287)

## 📊 Usage and capacity

- **Capacity card.** Count-based limits — documents and subgraphs — each get their own meter with a shared >80% warning rule owned by the API. Uncapped tiers show a plain count rather than a bar, and a tier with no subgraph allowance gets no row at all (#280, #283, #289)
- **Storage, itemized.** The Storage Usage card breaks the total down by type — graph, memory, subgraphs, vector indexes, staging — using data `/limits` was already returning and the page was discarding. "You are at 90%" becomes "you are at 90%, and most of it is staging," which is the version you can act on (#225)
- **The meter measures what the cap enforces.** Transient blue-green build artifacts are excluded from the headline figure, percentage and bar, so the bar no longer spikes toward 2× mid-rebuild while the warning colour stays calm. Build artifacts remain visible as their own breakdown row (#291)
- **Instance resources** — CPU and memory for dedicated graphs — are surfaced on the usage page (#223)
- Storage renders in a unit that can actually represent it, and subgraph sizes use byte-precise figures where the API provides them (#224, #290, #291)
- Tier and engine show as display names rather than raw tier strings (#230)

## 💾 Backups

- **Restore is retired from the customer surface.** Every graph type with an upstream rebuilds from that upstream — entity graphs re-materialize, generic graphs reload from staged sources, repositories re-ingest — and the archive only ever carried the derived database. What has no upstream is recovered by downloading the archive. The restore action, its modal and its operation monitoring are gone (#297, #299)
- **Encryption toggle removed.** Every completed backup is downloadable; the checkbox, the table column and the download-time guard are gone (#297)
- **Origin column.** Nightly platform backups appear alongside your own, badged `scheduled` or `manual`. This is load-bearing rather than decorative: only manual backups count against the tier's daily limit (#299)
- **Semantic Memory** in the backup details panel, as three states — _Included_, _None to include_, and _Not recorded_ for archives predating memory capture, which make no claim either way (#299)
- Retention is capped at the 90 days the API accepts, with helper text naming both the hard ceiling and the per-tier clamp (#238)

## 🧠 Memory & Knowledge Base

- **New `/memory` page.** The first UI over the semantic-memory API: browse, filter and paginate what agents have remembered, read provenance, edit or forget an entry, and run semantic recall as ranked, scored hits (#204)
- **One editor for both.** Memory and Knowledge Base editing share a Monaco markdown editor with a formatting toolbar and Write/Preview tabs, presented in a modal, with standardized tag and folder/type inputs and an unsaved-changes guard (#207)

## 💰 Pricing & content

- **Real prices on `/pricing`.** Dedicated graph tiers show $99 / $249 / $599 per graph with credits, subgraphs, storage and retention, and self-serve CTAs. Prices render from constants and reconcile against `/v1/offering`, so a repricing propagates without a frontend change — and a briefly unreachable API leaves a stale number rather than a blank card (#227)
- **Dedicated graphs lead the page,** with the SEC shared repository below, now that graph tiers are something a visitor can act on (#228)
- **A backups FAQ entry** covering the nightly schedule, the per-tier retention windows and daily on-demand allowance, and what a plan includes (#298)
- **Landing and platform pages refreshed** to the shipped product: the console demo rebuilt around the graph-aware AI analyst, schema chips corrected to real nodes, unimplemented integrations removed, and RoboLedger / RoboInvestor capability copy rewritten (#216, #219, #220)
- **Semantic sovereignty** introduced on the open-source surfaces, linking the defining essay (#240)
- **Live search on the research listing** (#209), a QuickBooks affiliate link in the integrations section (#202), and legal pages aligned with current positioning (#212)

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- **Graph switches no longer leak state across graphs.** Selections, open modals and delete confirmations are reset on a switch, and every data-loading page drops responses that arrive for the graph you just left. The worst case ran a preview query against the previous graph's table under the new graph's name (#232)
- **The subgraphs meter works for the first time.** Its endpoint had been shadowed by a route pattern for its entire life, failing silently inside `Promise.allSettled`; capacity now comes from `/limits` and drops a round-trip in the process (#289)
- **Billing reads are dropped on an org switch,** so the previous organization's customer record, subscriptions and invoices can no longer paint under the new one's name (#266)
- **Rate limits on the public contact and support forms now apply per visitor.** The client address is resolved from CloudFront's own record of the connection rather than inferred from proxy-hop counting, which had been throttling every visitor behind the edge as one (#231, #239)
- **Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon** loads as a classic script without a preload mismatch (#217, #218)
- Zeroed service-offering values are treated as missing rather than as data (#229)
- Research pages use query-shaped titles in search results (#237)

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **`/library` is gone.** The Taxonomy Library moves to RoboLedger, which already had the strict superset — it surfaced tenant-authored reporting extensions this copy filtered out. No capability is lost; the page is one app over (#226)
- **`/billing` is no longer a page.** It redirects to `/organization?tab=billing`. Bookmarks and inbound links keep working (#275)
- **Backup restore is no longer available in the UI** — download the archive instead (#299)

## 🔧 Infrastructure

- **Node 24 LTS runtime.** Builder and runner images, `.nvmrc`, `engines.node` and CI all move from Node 22, which has been in maintenance since October 2025 (#243)
- **`@robosystems/client` 0.4.0 → 1.7.0** across the series, including the 1.0 graduation. This app consumes the raw client, so each contract change landed as real call-site work rather than a lockfile bump (#200, #201, #236, #279, #284, #289, #291, #292, #293, #297, #299)
- **`@robosystems/core` 0.3.0 → 0.6.3**, carrying the shared search primitives, the console `/recall` verb, connector-URL generation, the scoped-key dialog and the password-change confirmation (#203, #205, #257, #264, #282, #284, #286, #294)
- **Zero open dependency advisories.** The high-severity postcss and sharp alerts were cleared, and a lockfile-only pass took `npm audit` to zero across the production tree (#241, #267, #296)
- **RFC 9116 `security.txt`**, referencing the Trust Center (#256, #258, #269)
- **Curated release notes.** `tag-release.yml` now uses a committed `.github/release-notes/v<version>.md` verbatim when one exists — this file is the first to use it — and the v1.0.0–v1.2.0 bodies were archived into the repo (#276, #277)
- Crawlers are kept off the authenticated app routes (#233); the npm CLI and nested package tarballs are pruned from the runtime image (#242, #268); OS packages are re-upgraded on every image build (#214); Dependabot updates are grouped with two blocked majors ignored (#261); Trivy SARIF only uploads when a scan produced one (#260)
- **Waitlist infrastructure removed** — the dead code path, the SNS topic and its CloudFormation resources, subscription and IAM grant. A stack update rides this deploy (#234, #235)

## 📦 Deploy notes

- **Deploy the API first.** The backups surface in this release reads `initiated_by` and `memory_included` from the backup list, which arrive with RoboFinSystems/robosystems #1113 and #1114 — merged to the API's `main` but not in v1.7.8. Until that ships, the Origin column reads `manual` for every row and Semantic Memory reads _Not recorded_; both are correct statements about a pre-nightly world, so the app degrades honestly rather than breaking. Backup downloads are also encoded correctly only from #1114 onward.
- Everything else in this release is served by API v1.7.8, already in production.
- The `WaitlistTopic` removal is a CloudFormation change to `cloudformation/template.yaml`; the app stack updates as part of the deploy.
- No new environment variables or GitHub Actions variables. `CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` was introduced and configured earlier in the v1.2 series.
